deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from cote 154 and the neighbouring pages): X is the real projective plane, viewed topologically as a surface carrying a system of pseudo-lines. Its orientation double cover is X~ = S^2. A pseudo-line Δ lifts to a 'great circle' Δ~ in S^2 that is stable under the antipodal map. D → D' is a specialization (degeneration) of a pseudo-line. D' passes through a vertex s, a crossing point of the arrangement. D is a nearby pseudo-line that, moving to D', sweeps across s.

Step 1. The fibre of X~ → X over s consists of two points. These are the two local orientations of X at s. The open arc Δ∖{s} is contractible, so it has a disc neighbourhood and is two-sided, even though Δ itself is one-sided. The page puts the two orientations at s in canonical bijection with the two banks ('rives') of Δ∖{s}. This works because the loop along Δ reverses orientation, so 'left bank for a given orientation' does not depend on the direction in which one leaves s.

Step 2. The specialization D → D' selects one bank of D'∖{s}: the one swept by the specialization.

Step 3. Main claim: there is a canonical combinatorial isomorphism between two 'combinatorial segments' (the transcription's 'ensembles combinatoires' should read 'segments combinatoires'; see corrections):
- the bank of specializations, i.e. the combinatorial data of the arrangement seen from the closure of the swept bank, as used by D;
- I(D',s), the 'cutting of D' at s', i.e. D'∖{s} considered as an interval carrying the ordered sequence of its crossings with the other pseudo-lines.

Step 4. Upstairs reading. s lifts to two antipodal points s~ and s~^- on D'~. These cut the circle D'~ into two arcs, each running from s~ to s~^-, and these correspond to the two orientations (banks). The antipodal map exchanges the two arcs. It reverses the cyclic orientation of the circle, so it sends the arc from s~ to s~^- onto the other arc from s~^- to s~ compatibly with the crossing data. This is the struck-out remark that it is a combinatorial isomorphism different from the identity. It therefore identifies both arcs combinatorially with one segment I(D',s). So whichever bank the specialization selects, one gets a well-defined canonical isomorphism 'rive des spécialisations de D utilisée ≅ I(D',s)'. This is recorded as the summary formula in the right margin.

Purpose. This serves the programme begun on the previous page (25.12): define a polyhedral structure Pol(D') on the set/space of pseudo-lines (or of combinatorial positions of an added pseudo-line), and compare Pol(D) with Pol(D') under specialization. The vertices of Δ correspond to vertices of Δ~ in the double cover. The page determines the local structure (a 'link') of the space of pseudo-lines at a specialization through a vertex s, in terms of the combinatorial segment I(D',s).
errors: The text is a heavily revised draft. Several attempted formulations of the antipodal identification are struck out and the final sentence trails off. The proof that the bank/specialization set is isomorphic to I(D',s) is asserted, not argued.
Minor terminological point: the orientation ↔ bank bijection at s needs the observation that Δ is one-sided, so the loop along Δ reverses orientation. This is not stated, but the claim is correct.

The precise meaning of 'spécialisation' and of the set being identified with I(D',s) is not defined on this page. It presumably means the face/cell structure traversed by D near s, but the page leaves it ambiguous.

ideas.what: Points of the orientation double cover S^2 → RP^2 over s identified with local orientations at s, and with the two banks of a pseudo-line minus s
ideas.modern_name: orientation double cover; lifting pseudo-line arrangements to pseudo-circle arrangements on S^2 (oriented matroid of rank 3)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical topology; Folkman–Lawrence (1978) topological representation of oriented matroids

ideas.what: Combinatorial segment I(D',s): the pseudo-line cut open at a vertex, with its ordered sequence of crossings
ideas.modern_name: local sequences / allowable sequences; cocircuit sequence along an element of a rank-3 oriented matroid

ideas.what: Canonical isomorphism between the set of specializations of a pseudo-line across vertex s (the swept bank) and I(D',s), with the antipodal map making the choice of bank irrelevant
ideas.modern_name: local structure of the extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid / mutations (triangle flips) and pencils of pseudo-lines through a vertex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Las Vergnas (localizations of single-element extensions, 1978); Sturmfels–Ziegler (extension spaces, 1993); Ringel (mutations, 1956)

missed.claim: Grothendieck is building a polyhedral structure Pol(D) on the space of (combinatorial positions of) pseudo-lines relative to an arrangement. He studies its local structure under specialization D → D' through a vertex via the canonical segment I(D',s). This is an early, independent approach to the extension space of rank-3 oriented matroids, whose topology later became a significant topic (the extension space conjecture, Mnëv–Ziegler). The thread is left unfinished here.
missed.quote: Rive des spécialisations de D utilisée ≅ I(D',s)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Using the double cover and antipodism to canonically identify the two banks gives a clean, orientation-free description of the link of a vertex in the extension/mutation complex. Historically this is an unrecorded independent entry of Grothendieck into oriented-matroid territory. Mathematically it seems mostly to recover known local facts.

deep.surprise_reason: A local, fragmentary lemma in Grothendieck's unpublished pseudo-line project. It is correct and neatly phrased via the double cover, but it is close to standard oriented-matroid / allowable-sequence combinatorics. Its interest is mainly historical, as part of an uncredited study of the space of pseudo-lines.
transcription_corrections: The opening should likely read 'Les pts de $\tilde\Delta$ au-dessus de s, i.e. les orientations de X en s', not 'de $\tilde{\Delta}_\infty$ [?] dessinés'. The two points of the double cover over s are the two local orientations.
'isom. combinatoire canonique entre les ensembles combinatoires correspondants' should read 'entre les segments combinatoires correspondants'.
The insertion reads roughly 'la rive des spécialisations correspondant à l'adhérence de la rive balayée de D, et celui correspondant à D', i.e. le découpage de D' en s'.
'deux arcs considérés comme deux arcs d'origine $\tilde s$, extrémité $\tilde s^-$': the arcs run from $\tilde s$ to the antipode $\tilde s^-$.
The marginal formula reads 'Rive des spécialisations de D utilisée $\xrightarrow{\sim} I(D',s)$', under the heading 'combinatoire canonique'.
